transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-20 15:00 PT | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood DevRel); Alex Kim (Northpoint), Maya Patel (Northpoint), Trevor Holmes (Northpoint)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — good afternoon. quick intro, I run partnerships for the West region here at Redwood Inference. we have Daniel who will run the dev walkthrough and Priya to show a couple quick console demos. 
[00:08] Alex: Hey Sofia, thanks. we are excited — we're trying to get a team of infra and ml folks aligned on how to integrate your SDKs for both python microservices and a TS edge worker. 
[00:15] Maya: yeah, timeline is pretty tight, we want a POC in the next three weeks.
[00:19] Daniel: cool. Goal for today: install SDKs, walk auth options (api keys, short-lived creds, SAML for console), demo the python quickstart, show typescript example for edge/worker, and then a short browse of the Console and Optimize suggestions. we'll leave time for Q&A and then list next steps. sound good?
[00:31] Trevor: Yep.

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Developer workshop on SDK setup and auth flows.
- Discussed hosted vs dedicated and the networking considerations for VPC deployments.
- Agreed to run a benchmark and share pricing.

Topics: SDK install, API auth, SSO/SAML, env vars, quickstarts (python & ts), Console route setup, Redwood Optimize recommendations, dedicated capacity notes.

[00:50] Daniel: alright I'm going to share my screen with a repo scaffold. First step: pip install redwood-inference (note: package name in pypi might be redwood-infer in some old docs — apologies if you hit that). so python: pip install redwood-inference==1.2.0rc. For node/TS it's npm i @redwood-inference/sdk or yarn add @redwood-inference/sdk.
[01:12] Alex: quick Q — we run inside a locked down container with no internet egress except to certain domains. what URLs do we need to allow?
[01:18] Daniel: good call out. for hosted API you'll need api.redwood.ai on 443 and auth.redwood.ai for token exchange, plus metrics endpoints to send telemetry if you enable them. For dedicated/private you will talk to your local control plane endpoint we’ll provide; that is the same host but under your VPC. Also the KV cache host is optional if you enable managed cache.
[01:35] Maya: any firewall IP ranges?
[01:37] Daniel: we publish a small set of ranges — I'll add that link in follow-up. (note: transcript may say 'range' or 'ranch' — docs link will be in the follow up).

[02:00] Daniel: Auth options: simplest is API keys set as REDWOOD_API_KEY or using the SDK's client builder with an apiKey argument. For short lived credentials, we support token exchange using a signed JWT from your identity provider — good for ephemeral workloads. For Console SSO and administrative flows we support SAML & SCIM for user provisioning.
[02:22] Priya: let me demo the Console quick: when you log in via SSO you get an org-level view. you can create a route, pin a model version, and enable Optimize suggestions — Optimize will give quantization and batching recommendations based on your route profile. sometimes our docs say 'Redwood Optimise' (british z) in older screenshots — ignore the spelling.
[02:45] Alex: Is Optimize automatic or do we opt in per route?
[02:48] Priya: Opt-in per route — we don't change serving behavior without approval. Optimize will surface a suggested config: e.g., batch_size 8 for conversational workloads, kv_cache enabled for prompt prefix reuse, and a quantization profile like 4bit-ptq for cheaper inference. it's advisory and you can test in staging.

[03:15] Daniel: Back to SDKs. I'm opening the python quickstart. file: examples/python/quickstart.py. core snippet: 

from redwood_inference import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate("Write a short support reply saying we received the ticket")
print(resp.text)

[03:36] Daniel: note: in older transcripts & docs we've seen 'redwood.infer' or 'redwoodclient' — those were older packages. Current SDK is redwood_inference and exports Client. small mismatch possible during pip search.
[03:45] Maya: for typescript, what does the API look like?
[03:48] Daniel: for TS it's similar. example: 

import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const res = await client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-70b', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'Summarize this...' } ] })

[04:10] Alex: do you have streaming examples? we need to stream tokens to our websocket service.
[04:14] Daniel: yes, both SDKs support streaming. Python has a stream() method that yields tokens; TS can use an event emitter or an async iterator depending on environment. Example link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/streaming (placeholder link, final link in follow up).

[04:40] [05:00] Maya: (interrupt) how do you handle rate limiting? we have different rate levels per service.
[05:02] Daniel: we surface rate limit headers and the SDK will backoff with jitter by default. you can override with your own retry/backoff policy in the client config. For dedicated customers we can set higher quotas and custom tokens.

[05:30] Trevor: For our security team, can you outline data retention and encryption at rest?
[05:35] Sofia: yes. hosted api — data retention defaults to 30 days for telemetry unless you opt out; for enterprise/dedicated we have configuration to disable retention and enable customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). We'll attach the SOC 2 and encryption docs.
[05:51] Alex: do you support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) for private?
[05:54] Sofia: yes, BYOK via KMS in private deployments — customer keeps control. details in the compliance pack.

[06:15] Daniel: back to installing in CI: recommended pattern is to set REDWOOD_API_KEY as a secret and to pin SDK versions. For pull-request checks we suggest using a lightweight sandbox model or a local mock server we provide in the repo to avoid throttling. There's a small npm package @redwood-inference/mock-server for local tests.
[06:38] Maya: are there official terraform modules or Helm charts for private install?
[06:41] Daniel: yes — we maintain a Helm chart repo and a terraform module for the control plane and routing. I'll share links. For on-prem you can deploy with the helm chart and pass in your ingress & KMS configs.

[07:10] Daniel: demo time — I'll run the python quickstart inside a container. (terminal noise)
[07:15] Terminal: [pip installing redwood-inference 1.2.0rc...]
[07:22] Terminal: Warning: legacy package redwood-infer found on local index, using redwood_inference.
[07:30] [08:00] Daniel: Running quickstart now... sending 3 sample prompts. (you'll hear keyboard)
[08:12] Daniel: output looks good — one caveat: if your prompt lengths exceed model context tokens you'll see truncation. Use the SDK's streaming and a chunked upload pattern for very large documents.

[09:00] Alex: For embeddings, we want deterministic vectors for nearest-neighbors. any known nondeterminism?
[09:05] Daniel: embeddings are deterministic for the same model/version and input. if you pick a different model or quantized variant you may see small differences. Optimize will flag when embedding regression occurs between versions.

[09:40] Priya: I'm jumping into the Console route setup — show a Route create flow. you can set model, temperature, max tokens, batching and cache policies. we recommend enabling prefix KV cache for chat history reuse in conversation routes. Screenshot link: https://console.redwood.ai/org/abc/routes/quickstart (placeholder).
[10:05] Maya: is there a JSON schema for route definitions?
[10:08] Priya: yes, route config is JSON. Example: {"model":"redwood-7b","batching":{"enabled":true,"max_batch":8},"cache":{"prefix_kv":true}} — I'll attach the exact schema in follow up.

[10:30] Daniel: Let's talk about environment setup patterns. We usually see two patterns: 1) microservice pattern: server-side python/Go/Node worker with a pinned API key and possibly VPC egress and private link; 2) edge-augmenter pattern: TS edge function that calls a proxy you control which holds the API key, so you never put keys in the browser. We avoid shipping API keys to browsers.
[10:58] Trevor: we plan to have edge inference for low-latency autocomplete. any recommended approach?
[11:02] Daniel: for ultra low latency consider using a nearby dedicated pool in the same cloud region + model sharding; or host a small local model for first-pass and call Redwood for heavier hallucination-proofing. Also use streaming for incremental tokens.

[11:30] [12:00] Alex: security question — we run strict SAML SSO and SCIM. How granular is RBAC within Console?
[12:05] Sofia: you can define org roles and route-level permissions; we support SAML groups mapped to roles, and SCIM for user provisioning. audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private with longer retention options.

[12:35] Daniel: I want to demo a quick typescript snippet that shows streaming to a websocket. code: 

import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://myservice/ws')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
for await (const token of client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-7b', messages: [...] })) {
  ws.send(token)
}

[12:58] Maya: the 'for await' idiom is great. we'll likely wrap that in a backpressure aware queue.

[13:20] Trevor: can the SDK run in a FIPS environment?
[13:23] Daniel: current SDK doesn't ship a FIPS-only crypto layer by default; for Private deployments we can provide a FIPS-compatible build or guidance to link against your FIPS lib. I'll add that as an item.

[13:45] Alex: about Dedicated vs Hosted: we care about SLA and predictable latency. any numbers you can share?
[13:50] Sofia: for hosted we have p50 latency numbers on the catalog for each model (example redwood-7b ~110ms p50 on 8k context under default batching), but for customers needing consistency we recommend Dedicated capacity where we can hit tighter SLOs — we'll share the benchmark spreadsheets.

[14:20] Daniel: one more quick dev note: caching semantics — prefix KV cache is per-route and eviction is LRU; you can set a TTL. Also request-level caching is useful for idempotent queries.

[15:00] Alex: Anything special about types/ts typings? we need good DX for our engineers.
[15:03] Priya: yep, the TS SDK is fully typed and ships with generated types for models and responses. we also publish an OpenAPI spec and a small codegen helper to generate client stubs for internal services.

[15:30] Daniel: Open Q: any blocking items from your side?
[15:33] Alex: two blockers: 1) Security needs SOC2 + BYOK docs, 2) Infra wants a short benchmark in our region to measure p95.
[15:42] Sofia: we will send SOC2 & encryption pack, and we'll run a benchmark with Trevor.

[16:00] Q&A rapid fire:
[16:03] Maya: Can we run private control plane in AWS GovCloud?
[16:06] Sofia: yes, private deployments in GovCloud are supported via our on-prem package — we will need to validate compliance specifics.

[16:20] Trevor: Who owns the model upgrades if we pin a version?
[16:23] Daniel: you pin model versions per route — you choose when to upgrade. Optimize will alert you to quality regressions between versions.

[16:40] Alex: What about on-prem GPU drivers and kernel versions?
[16:43] Daniel: our runtime supports a range of CUDA/cuDNN versions; we publish a compatibility matrix. For older kernels we provide a compatibility shim.

[17:00] Priya: Demo wrap: console quick check: you can run a live test request in the console, inspect tokens, and download traces. that trace links back to the route and the model version used.

[17:30] Sofia: Ok, recap & next steps: Daniel will send a python quickstart benchmark script and a TS streaming example. I'll share pricing and SOC2/compliance docs. Trevor will provision a test account & VPC topology so we can run a dedicated vs hosted benchmark. We'll aim to reconvene after the benchmark.

[17:50] Alex: sounds good. Thanks, everyone.
[17:55] Daniel: thanks — we'll follow up with the repo links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples (placeholder), and a short support doc: https://redwood.example.com/support/sdk-quickstart.

[18:10] End of transcript notes: transcription had some mis-heard package names and a couple of speaker label swaps around 07:00-08:00 when multiple people spoke. references to 'Optimize' spelled 'Optimise' in older screenshots; "redwood-infer" vs "redwood_inference" package confusion noted.
